stableFactsAndClaims: Arrangement A puts labels at the front edge; B puts them above the relevant shelf.
Twelve participants each performed one search under each arrangement; order alternated between participants.
Median times were 19 seconds for A and 24 seconds for B.
No uncertainty interval was calculated; participants were staff familiar with the room.
The task used one deliberately misplaced label, unlike ordinary searches that may involve multiple labels, unfamiliar categories, or interruptions.
The results support a further trial, not broad superiority; visitors would test whether the observed difference extends to unfamiliar users.
